graph.title: Arduino Zero Simple Audio Frequency Meter (LMV358 non-inverting amplifier)
notes: The catalogue entry opamp-lmv358 has an empty port list, so no port on it can be referenced. That caused the V4 errors. I created a new part type, lmv358-dip8, with numbered lead ports 1-8 and used it for ic1. This is not a different part from the manual's LMV358. It is the same chip with its pins defined.

lmv358-dip8 pin numbering follows the standard dual op-amp pinout: 1 OUT A, 2 IN A-, 3 IN A+, 4 GND, 5 IN B+, 6 IN B-, 7 OUT B, 8 V+. Its 'through' list only records the signal paths from inputs to outputs.
On the breadboard the chip straddles the centre gap in columns 14-17, with pin 1 at 14t.e and pin 8 at 14b.f.
The Arduino Zero is not in the catalogue, so it is a new part type. It is powered over USB, which the manual doesn't draw.
The op-amp's Vcc comes from the IOREF pin (3.3 V on the Zero), as in both images.
The catalogue match for the 100 nF capacitor (capacitor-10uf, polarized) is wrong. The image shows a non-polarized ceramic disc, so I created capacitor-100nf.
The catalogue match for the 3.5 mm jack (midi-jack) is wrong, so I created audio-jack-35mm with SLEEVE, RIGHT and LEFT lugs, as in the schematic. Only SLEEVE and RIGHT are wired. LEFT is unused.

Breadboard row letters follow the image: rows a-e are the lower half (bank 't') and rows f-j are the upper half (bank 'b'). Rails: tp is the top red rail, bn is the bottom blue (negative) rail. Holes are numbered 1-25 along each rail, skipping the gaps.
The teal jumper in row C is drawn ending near column 14, which is the op-amp output strip. The schematic puts the R10/R11 node on the inverting input (pin 2, column 15), so I wired it 10t.c to 15t.c.

The trimmer is read as outer pins at 1t.e (GND) and 3t.e (VCC), and the wiper at 2b.f. The purple wire from 2b.g carries the wiper to the op-amp output (14t.d). R11 attaches to the trimmer's column-3 terminal.

Resistor values come from the schematic: R8 and R9 are 100k, and R10 and R11 are 47k. R8 runs from the Vcc column 12 to the + input at column 16. R9 runs from column 16 to the GND column 20. R10 runs from GND (column 6) to the - input node (column 10). R11 runs from the trimmer to the - input node (column 7, tied to column 10 by a jumper).
Wire ends to the jack lugs are assumed to be soldered. The jack is a breakout board, and the manual doesn't say how they attach.
